name: motion-number-input
title: Animated Number Input
description: A stack of labelled rows for Adults, Children and Rooms, each with a minus and plus button around a large number. Pressing a button or typing changes the figure with a rolling digit animation.
use: A booking or order form needs small bounded quantities like guests, rooms or tickets entered quickly.
avoid: The plus and minus buttons are aria-hidden and skipped by tab, so only the unnamed number field is reachable.
a11y: The minus and plus buttons are aria-hidden and skipped by tab, the number field has no label, and its outline is suppressed. (keyboard: partial, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark rounded card divided into three rows. Each row carries a bold label and a small grey hint on the left, and on the right a strip of minus sign, large white number and plus sign.
behaves: Pressing minus or plus steps the number within its bounds and the digits roll vertically to the new value; typing into the field does the same. A sign greys out once its limit is reached.
customise: Supply value, min, max and a change handler; size, colours and digit font come from classes, and the labelled rows are built around it.
weight: light: Three small steppers with animated digits; no canvas or loop.
demo: Rows Adults (Ages 13 or above), Children (Ages 2 to 12), Rooms (Up to 9 per booking), starting at 2, 1 and 1.
issues: The minus and plus buttons are aria-hidden and not tabbable, so they cannot be used from the keyboard.
Frames 2 to 5 catch half-rolled digits that look broken as stills.
polishWhy: Tidy rows and smooth digit rolls, but the controls themselves look like default steppers.
